title_english: Policy for Development of Renewable Energy for Power Generation, 2006
summary_english: Earlier federal policy for renewable power generation under which wind and solar IPPs were procured on cost-plus or upfront tariffs. It was succeeded by the Alternative and Renewable Energy Policy 2019.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Included only as the predecessor of the ARE Policy 2019; date and title from general knowledge and the AEDB guide's reference to the 'Renewable Energy Act of 2006' (sic). Verify title, date and the succession clause.

issuing_body: Council of Common Interests; Ministry of Energy (Power Division); AEDB
title_original: Alternative and Renewable Energy Policy 2019
title_english: Alternative and Renewable Energy Policy 2019
summary_english: Sets targets for alternative and renewable energy of 20% of generation capacity by 2025 and 30% by 2030 and moves procurement of new projects to competitive bidding in place of cost-plus or upfront tariffs. It also provides incentives for local manufacturing of solar panels and wind turbines, including customs duty exemptions on equipment and materials.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Targets and features from Dawn (2020-08-13, announcement after CCI approval) and climate-laws.org; CCI approval date not found (a CCI meeting on 2019-12-23 was expected to consider it). Also referred to as ARE Policy 2020. Policy PDF copy at rise.esmap.org.

title_original: National Electricity Policy 2021
title_english: National Electricity Policy 2021
summary_english: Policy issued under section 14A of the NEPRA Act that sets objectives for generation, transmission, distribution and market development and requires a National Electricity Plan to implement it.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). CCI approval on 2021-06-21 per Dawn, Radio Pakistan and others; gazette date not found. Copy of the text at icimod.org. National Electricity Plan 2023-27 not confirmed.

issuing_body: Independent System and Market Operator (ISMO); approved by NEPRA
title_original: Indicative Generation Capacity Expansion Plan 2025-35 (Integrated System Plan 2025-35)
title_english: Indicative Generation Capacity Expansion Plan 2025-35 (Integrated System Plan 2025-35)
summary_english: Least-cost generation expansion plan prepared by the system operator for the 2025-2035 period and filed with NEPRA. Secondary reports say NEPRA approved the Integrated System Plan 2025-35 comprising the revised recommended case of IGCEP 2025, excluding battery storage and a K-Electric transmission line in 2028.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Linked file is the August 2025 filing (R2) on NEPRA's site; NEPRA posted addenda to ISP 2025-35 in July 2026. Approval date and decision not found; earlier IGCEP 2022-31 not recorded. Confirm status and date from the NEPRA decision.

number: unnumbered (NEPRA declaration of commercial market operation date)
title_original: Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM): start of commercial market operations
title_english: Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM): start of commercial market operations
summary_english: NEPRA declared 2026-01-22 as the start of commercial operations of the Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market, the wholesale market in which eligible buyers and suppliers trade under bilateral contracts, with the Independent System and Market Operator as market operator. A NEPRA determination in October 2025 had cleared the final test run and the Market Commercial Code.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Dates from Business Recorder and Express Tribune reports (secondary); the NEPRA decision document was not located. NEPRA's original approval of the CTBCM design (around 2020) and the Market Commercial Code are candidates for separate rows.

number: unnumbered (NEPRA approval of ISMO wheeling auction framework)
issuing_body: National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA); Independent System and Market Operator (ISMO)
title_original: Competitive electricity wheeling auction mechanism (Framework Guidelines for Wheeling Auctions)
title_english: Competitive electricity wheeling auction mechanism (Framework Guidelines for Wheeling Auctions)
summary_english: NEPRA approved an auction framework submitted by ISMO that allocates up to 800 MW of demand for wheeling under the CTBCM, with a minimum load of 1 MW per participant and a cap of 20% (160 MW) for any bidder or affiliated group. It builds on Framework Guidelines for Wheeling Auctions issued on 2026-01-22.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). From Profit (Pakistan Today), 2026-03-25 (secondary); approval date and NEPRA decision number not found. The article also cites amendments to the National Electricity Plan and supplier licensing rules notified in August 2025 (not recorded). NEPRA's site lists an ISMO wheeling auction notice (July 2026).

title_original: National Electric Vehicle Policy 2019
title_english: National Electric Vehicle Policy 2019
summary_english: First national policy for electric vehicles, approved by the Federal Cabinet, with incentives for EV manufacturing and purchase. It targeted conversion of 100,000 cars and 500,000 two- and three-wheelers to electric within four years.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Cabinet approval 2019-11-05 per Profit and Arab News (secondary). In June 2020 a two- and three-wheeler phase was approved for implementation with cars deferred (Dawn). Status 'replaced' assumes the NEV Policy 2025-30 succeeds it; confirm. Ministry site unreachable from our client.

title_original: New Energy Vehicle Policy 2025-30
title_english: New Energy Vehicle Policy 2025-30
summary_english: Sets a target of 30% electric vehicles in new vehicle sales by 2030, with subsidies for electric two- and three-wheelers (Rs9 billion for FY2025-26), motorway charging stations and charging requirements in building codes. It provides customs duty and sales tax exemptions on EV parts.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Launch on Thursday 2025-06-19 per Dawn (2025-06-20); one report says Federal Cabinet approval on 26 August (year unclear). Longer-term targets and a petrol-vehicle levy are reported inconsistently and were left out. Official text not located.

short_name: Finance Act 2024 (solar, inverter and battery manufacturing inputs)
title_original: Finance Act, 2024 (Customs Act Fifth Schedule entries for solar panel, inverter and battery manufacturing)
title_english: Finance Act, 2024 (Customs Act Fifth Schedule entries for solar panel, inverter and battery manufacturing)
summary_english: Through amendments to the Fifth Schedule of the Customs Act, sets 0% customs duty on specified machinery and equipment imported by manufacturers of solar panels, solar inverters and solar batteries, and on specified inverter and lithium battery parts imported by registered local assemblers, subject to quota and conditions.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Entries from the FBR Finance Bill 2024 Notes on Clauses and budget speech coverage; assent 2024-06-29 per KPMG brief. The enacted Fifth Schedule serial numbers were not checked; Finance Acts have no running number in this sense.

short_name: Finance Act 2025 (sales tax on imported solar panels)
title_original: Finance Act, 2025 (Sales Tax Act amendments on imported solar panels)
title_english: Finance Act, 2025 (Sales Tax Act amendments on imported solar panels)
summary_english: Removes the sales tax exemption for solar panels at serial 164 of Table-1 of the Sixth Schedule to the Sales Tax Act, 1990 and applies a reduced 10% sales tax to imported solar panels; the Finance Bill had proposed 18%.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Linked URL is FBR Sales Tax Circular No. 02 of 2025-26 (2025-08-02) explaining the Finance Act 2025, not the Act itself; our text extraction got only the first page, so the solar paragraph was taken from a search summary of the circular. Reports conflict on scope (assembled panels vs components); check the Eighth Schedule entry.

title_original: বাংলাদেশ এনার্জি রেগুলেটরী কমিশন আইন, ২০০৩
title_english: Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission Act, 2003
summary_english: Establishes the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission as an independent regulator for electricity, gas and petroleum products, with powers to issue licences and determine tariffs after public hearing.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Number and date read from bdlaws (HTTP 200). Also amended by Act No. 25 of 2020 (not recorded).

title_original: বাংলাদেশ এনার্জি রেগুলেটরী কমিশন (সংশোধন) আইন, ২০২৩
title_english: Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (Amendment) Act, 2023
summary_english: Amends section 34 of the BERC Act and inserts section 34A, allowing the government to fix or adjust electricity, gas and fuel tariffs in special cases without a BERC public hearing. It enacted an ordinance of December 2022.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Number, date and section list read from bdlaws. Section 34A was removed by Ordinance 7/2024 and then by Act 40/2026; status 'amended' because the section 34 changes may remain - check.

title_original: বাংলাদেশ এনার্জি রেগুলেটরী কমিশন (সংশোধন) অধ্যাদেশ, ২০২৪
title_english: Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 2024
summary_english: Deletes section 34A of the BERC Act, ending the government's power to set energy tariffs without the Commission, so price changes again go through BERC with a public hearing.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Read from bdlaws: issued under Art. 93(1) while Parliament was dissolved; bdlaws marks it repealed by Act No. 40 of 2026.

title_original: বাংলাদেশ এনার্জি রেগুলেটরী কমিশন (সংশোধন) আইন, ২০২৬
title_english: Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (Amendment) Act, 2026
summary_english: Enacts by Act of Parliament the deletion of section 34A of the BERC Act and repeals Ordinance No. 7 of 2024 with savings.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Date and section headings read from bdlaws; check commencement clause (s. 1) for whether it applies retrospectively from 2024-08-27.

short_name: Quick Enhancement of Electricity and Energy Supply (Special Provisions) Act 2010
title_original: বিদ্যুৎ ও জ্বালানীর দ্রুত সরবরাহ বৃদ্ধি (বিশেষ বিধান) আইন, ২০১০
title_english: Quick Enhancement of Electricity and Energy Supply (Special Provisions) Act, 2010
summary_english: Allowed the government to procure power plants and energy supply through negotiated contracts outside normal tender procedures and limited legal challenge to actions taken under it. Its term was extended by later amendments, including Act No. 22 of 2021.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Number, date and repeal read from bdlaws. Content summary from secondary sources (immunity clause s. 9 struck down by the High Court on 2024-11-14 per press).

title_original: বিদ্যুৎ ও জ্বালানীর দ্রুত সরবরাহ বৃদ্ধি (বিশেষ বিধান) (রহিতকরণ) অধ্যাদেশ, ২০২৪
title_english: Quick Enhancement of Electricity and Energy Supply (Special Provisions) (Repeal) Ordinance, 2024
summary_english: Repeals the 2010 special provisions act while saving agreements made and actions taken under it before repeal.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Read from bdlaws; marked there as repealed by Act No. 18 of 2026. Savings clause per press reports.

title_original: বিদ্যুৎ ও জ্বালানীর দ্রুত সরবরাহ বৃদ্ধি (বিশেষ বিধান) (রহিতকরণ) আইন, ২০২৬
title_english: Quick Enhancement of Electricity and Energy Supply (Special Provisions) (Repeal) Act, 2026
summary_english: Repeals Act No. 54 of 2010 with savings by Act of Parliament and repeals Ordinance No. 15 of 2024.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Read from bdlaws (section headings only).

title_original: বিদ্যুৎ আইন, ২০১৮
title_english: Electricity Act, 2018
summary_english: Repeals and re-enacts the Electricity Act 1910 to govern generation, transmission, supply and distribution, and provides for an Independent System Operator.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Number, date and table of contents read from bdlaws.

title_original: টেকসই ও নবায়নযোগ্য জ্বালানি উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষ আইন, ২০১২
title_english: Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority Act, 2012
summary_english: Establishes the Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority (SREDA) to promote renewable energy and energy efficiency and conservation.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Pre-2015; included because SREDA administers the net metering guidelines and the 2026 solar ordinance. Number and date from bdlaws.

issuing_body: Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources (Power Division)
title_original: Renewable Energy Policy of Bangladesh, 2008
title_english: Renewable Energy Policy of Bangladesh, 2008
summary_english: First national renewable energy policy, which set a target of 5% of power demand from renewables by 2015 and 10% by 2020 and provided fiscal incentives for renewable energy equipment. It was repealed by the Renewable Energy Policy 2025.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Included as predecessor; targets and date from general knowledge, repeal per Chambers 2025. Verify text and exact date.

issuing_body: Advisory Council; Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources (Power Division)
title_original: Renewable Energy Policy 2025
title_english: Renewable Energy Policy 2025
summary_english: Sets targets for renewable energy of 20% of electricity by 2030 and 30% by 2040 and replaces the 2008 policy. Secondary sources report capacity targets of 6,145 MW by 2030 and 17,470 MW by 2041.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Advisory Council approval 2025-05-06 (Dhaka Tribune); published on the Power Division site in June 2025 (Daily Star, Daily Sun 2025-06-16). Sources differ between 2040 and 2041 for the 30% target. Language of the binding text not confirmed (may be bn).

issuing_body: Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources (Power Division)
title_original: Net Metering Guidelines 2018
title_english: Net Metering Guidelines 2018
summary_english: Allowed three-phase consumers to connect rooftop solar to the distribution grid under net metering, capped as a share of sanctioned load, with surplus energy credited against later consumption.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Approval date per IEEFA (others say July 2018 or later); revised in 2019 (not recorded). URL is an ESMAP copy of the English translation (November 2018 cover). 70% sanctioned-load cap per press. Official Bengali text on SREDA/Power Division not reached (SREDA TLS error).

issuing_body: Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources (Power Division)
title_original: Net Metering Guideline 2025
title_english: Net Metering Guideline 2025
summary_english: Replaces the 2018 guidelines, raising the cap for net-metered rooftop solar to 100% of sanctioned load and opening net metering to single-phase consumers.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Month from bdnews24 and pv magazine (secondary); official text not located. Check exact issue date and whether it expressly replaces the 2018/2019 guidelines.

number: unnumbered (Power Division circular, National Rooftop Solar Programme)
issuing_body: Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources (Power Division)
title_original: National Rooftop Solar Programme (circular and implementation guideline)
title_english: National Rooftop Solar Programme (circular and implementation guideline)
summary_english: Directs installation of rooftop solar on government offices, educational institutions and hospitals, with a reported aim of about 3,000 MW by December 2025. Government offices use a publicly funded capex model and hospitals and educational institutions an opex model through service providers.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Announcement 2025-07-03 (CPD) and circular 2025-07-07 (TBS); a 'National Rooftop Solar Programme Implementation Guideline' is cited by Chambers. Official circular not located; language assumed bn.

title_original: বিশেষ সৌরবিদ্যুৎ স্থাপন অধ্যাদেশ, ২০২৬
title_english: Special Solar Power Installation Ordinance, 2026
summary_english: Makes special provisions to speed up installation of 'special solar power' systems, including tripartite agreements, special procurement provisions, SREDA record-keeping and monitoring, a net-metering incentive, and a National Policy Council and local coordination committees. It also creates offences for theft of or damage to such systems and obstruction of installation.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Number, date (2026-10-19) and section headings read from bdlaws; issued under Art. 93(1) while Parliament was not in session, so it lapses unless laid before and approved by Parliament. Substantive provisions (which installations qualify) were not read; check sections 2-9.

short_name: Integrated Energy and Power Master Plan 2023
issuing_body: Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources
title_original: Integrated Energy and Power Master Plan (IEPMP) 2023
title_english: Integrated Energy and Power Master Plan (IEPMP) 2023
summary_english: Long-term plan for the energy and power sector up to 2050, prepared with Japanese assistance, covering demand, generation mix, fuels and grid. The interim government has prepared a draft 25-year Energy and Power Sector Master Plan for 2026-2050 intended to succeed it.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Approved in 2023; one source says published 2023-11-27 (not confirmed). Status of the draft successor plan (Daily Star, Financial Express, CPD 2025-26) unclear; if adopted, mark this row replaced. JICA role from general knowledge.

title_original: Electric Motor Vehicle Registration and Operation Guidelines 2023
title_english: Electric Motor Vehicle Registration and Operation Guidelines 2023
summary_english: Sets rules for registering and operating electric motor vehicles, allowing them to be registered with the road transport authority (BRTA) and used on roads.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Gazette date 2023-04-18 from two Financial Express reports; the name varies (Guideline/Policy/Movement). Issuing division assumed; BRTA site unreachable from our client. Charging station guidelines (Power Division) are a candidate for a separate row.

issuing_body: National Board of Revenue (Internal Resources Division)
title_original: Customs exemption notification for solar power equipment (SRO No. 159-Law/2026/14-Customs)
title_english: Customs exemption notification for solar power equipment (SRO No. 159-Law/2026/14-Customs)
summary_english: Exempts specified solar power equipment from customs duty, regulatory duty and advance tax, as announced in the FY2026-27 budget. Press reports say eligibility was initially limited mainly to VAT-registered renewable energy service companies and later extended to commercial importers.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). SRO number and date from Financial Express; text not read. Later NBR changes (extension to commercial importers; the September 2026 1% notification) may have amended it; check the HS codes, conditions and any amending SROs.

short_name: Solar equipment import tax cut to 1% (180 days)
issuing_body: National Board of Revenue (Internal Resources Division)
title_original: NBR notification reducing total import taxes on solar equipment to 1% for 180 days
title_english: NBR notification reducing total import taxes on solar equipment to 1% for 180 days
summary_english: For 180 days, exempts listed solar equipment, including PV modules, inverters, mounting structures, battery management and thermal management systems and monitoring equipment, from customs duty, VAT, regulatory and supplementary duty and advance tax, leaving a total incidence reported as 1%.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). From pv magazine (2026-09-18) and Financial Express; SRO number and date not found. It may amend SRO 159 or stand alone; not linked. Time-limited: check expiry (about March 2027).

issuing_body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title_original: Mujib Climate Prosperity Plan 2022-2041
title_english: Mujib Climate Prosperity Plan 2022-2041
summary_english: Climate and development investment plan, unveiled in 2021, that sets out a pathway for climate-resilient, low-carbon growth including expanded renewable energy, with investment needs reported at about US$80-90 billion.
notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Document title and 2022 cover per MoEFCC PDF (not fetched; moef.portal.gov.bd unreachable). Status after August 2024 unconfirmed: CPD listed it for reform, and no formal withdrawal was found. Reviewer should decide whether it is still in force.

issuing_body: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
title_original: 全国人民代表大会常务委员会关于修改《中华人民共和国电力法》等四部法律的决定
title_english: Decision of the NPC Standing Committee on Amending the Electricity Law of the PRC and Three Other Laws
summary_english: Amends Article 25(3) of the Electricity Law of 1995 so that supply business areas are approved by the electricity administration together with other departments, with an electricity business licence issued on approval. The Electricity Law, as amended in 2009, 2015 and 2018, remains the framework law for generation, grid operation, supply and pricing.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Date and order number come from consolidated texts and law-database summaries found by web search; the National Laws and Regulations Database (flk.npc.gov.cn) did not answer, so the official text was not read. The 1995 base law (adopted 1995-12-28 per general knowledge) and the 2009 and 2015 amendments are not recorded as rows; a revision of the Electricity Law was on the State Council 2025 legislative plan, but no draft submission to the NPCSC was found.

number: unnumbered (NPCSC amending decision of 2009-12-26; presidential order number not confirmed)
issuing_body: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
title_original: 全国人民代表大会常务委员会关于修改《中华人民共和国可再生能源法》的决定
title_english: Decision of the NPC Standing Committee on Amending the Renewable Energy Law of the PRC
summary_english: Amends the Renewable Energy Law of 2005, requiring a national renewable energy development plan with total and medium- to long-term targets. It places the grid companies' obligation to purchase renewable electricity within that plan and provides for a renewable energy development fund.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Dates confirmed from the MEE-hosted consolidated text and law databases; the fund provision is from general knowledge and must be checked. The 2005 base law is not recorded as a row. A full revision (CN-BILL-2026-RE) had its first NPCSC reading in November 2026.

number: unnumbered (revision draft, first reading at the 25th session of the 14th NPCSC)
issuing_body: State Council (submitting); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
title_original: 中华人民共和国可再生能源法（修订草案）
title_english: Renewable Energy Law of the PRC (Revision Draft)
summary_english: A draft full revision of the Renewable Energy Law in ten chapters and 76 articles, submitted for first reading on 2026-11-02. As reported, it provides for a unified national electricity market, a price settlement mechanism for renewable generation, consumption responsibility weights, green electricity certificates and recycling of retired wind and solar equipment.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Content from Xinhua and Guangming reports of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-04; the draft text on npc.gov.cn was not found. date_in_force left empty because the bill is not adopted (departs from the spec). Link to CN-LAW-2009-RE-AMEND once adopted.

issuing_body: National Development and Reform Commission; National Energy Administration
title_original: 国家发展改革委 国家能源局关于深化新能源上网电价市场化改革 促进新能源高质量发展的通知
title_english: Notice on Deepening Market-Based Reform of On-Grid Tariffs for New Energy to Promote High-Quality Development of New Energy
summary_english: Requires all wind and solar output to enter the electricity market, with on-grid prices formed by market trading, and sets up a price settlement ('mechanism price') for a share of output. Projects commissioned before 2025-06-01 keep a mechanism price not above the local coal benchmark; for projects commissioned from 2025-06-01 the mechanism price is set by competitive bidding under a provincial ceiling. Provinces were to issue implementation plans by the end of 2025.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Official page read: signed 2025-01-27, published 2025-02-09; the text states no general effective date, so date_in_force is the publication date and 2025-06-01 is the cut-off between existing and new projects. Check whether it supersedes the 2021 parity-pricing notice 发改价格〔2021〕833号 (not recorded).

title_original: 国家能源局关于印发《分布式光伏发电开发建设管理办法》的通知
title_english: Notice on Issuing the Measures for the Administration of Development and Construction of Distributed Photovoltaic Power Generation
summary_english: Replaces the 2013 interim measures on distributed PV and classifies projects as residential (individual), residential (non-individual), general commercial and industrial, and large commercial and industrial. It sets filing (备案) rules, grid-connection procedures and registration after connection; projects filed before issue and connected before 2025-05-01 keep the previous policy.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Issued as a normative document (规范性文件) of the NEA, mapped to ministerial regulation; valid five years per secondary sources. Xinhua gives 2025-01-23 as the issue date, gov.cn and local copies 2025-01-17: check the date on the official text. Revokes 国能新能〔2013〕433号 (not recorded).

issuing_body: National Development and Reform Commission; Ministry of Finance; National Energy Administration
title_original: 国家发展改革委 财政部 国家能源局关于做好可再生能源绿色电力证书全覆盖工作 促进可再生能源电力消费的通知
title_english: Notice on Full Coverage of Renewable Energy Green Electricity Certificates to Promote Renewable Electricity Consumption
summary_english: Extends green electricity certificates from onshore wind and utility-scale solar to all registered renewable generation projects and makes the certificate the basis for proving renewable electricity consumption. It sets rules on issuance, trading and use of certificates.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Published on ndrc.gov.cn 2023-08-03; the signing date was not confirmed (one bank note gives 2023-07-25). Implementing rules: NEA 国能发新能规〔2024〕67号 of 2024-08-26 on certificate issuance and trading (not recorded).

issuing_body: National Development and Reform Commission; National Energy Administration
title_original: 国家发展改革委 国家能源局关于加快推动新型储能发展的指导意见
title_english: Guiding Opinions on Accelerating the Development of New-Type Energy Storage
summary_english: Sets a target of more than 30 GW of new-type (non-pumped-hydro) energy storage by 2025 and full market-based development by 2030. It covers planning, market participation and pricing mechanisms for storage.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Signing date 2021-07-15 from gov.cn metadata; published 2021-07-23. Later instruments (NEA 国能发科技规〔2021〕47号 project management rules; 2022 notice on independent storage in markets) not recorded.

issuing_body: National Development and Reform Commission; National Energy Administration
title_original: 国家发展改革委 国家能源局关于印发《“十四五”现代能源体系规划》的通知
title_english: 14th Five-Year Plan for a Modern Energy System
summary_english: The national energy plan for 2021-2025, approved by the State Council. It sets 2025 targets including total generating capacity of about 3,000 GW and a non-fossil share of energy consumption of about 20%.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Signed 2022-01-29, published 2022-03-22/23. Target figures come from media summaries; check against the plan text. The 15th Five-Year energy plans (2026-2030) were not searched.

issuing_body: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
title_original: 中华人民共和国能源法
title_english: Energy Law of the PRC
summary_english: China's first comprehensive energy law, in nine chapters and 80 articles covering energy planning, development and use, the energy market system, reserves and emergency response, technology innovation and supervision. It includes provisions on demand response by energy users.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Presidential Order No. 37 of 2024-11-08 confirmed on gov.cn and npc.gov.cn listings; in force 2025-01-01. Check whether it treats hydrogen as energy (reported by secondary sources, not confirmed here).

short_name: Interim Regulations on Carbon Emission Trading
title_original: 碳排放权交易管理暂行条例
title_english: Interim Regulations on the Administration of Carbon Emission Trading
summary_english: Establishes the national carbon emission trading market by administrative regulation, covering allowance allocation and surrender, registration and trading institutions, and verification of emission reports. It prohibits the creation of new local carbon markets.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Amended by State Council Order No. 843 (decision of 2026-08-08, in force 2026-08-15), which revised the penalty for failure to surrender allowances in Article 24; not recorded as a row. Earlier ministerial basis: MEE Order No. 19, Measures for the Administration of Carbon Emission Trading (Trial), 2020-12-31, in force 2021-02-01 (not recorded).

short_name: ETS extension to steel, cement, aluminium

title_original: 财政部 税务总局 工业和信息化部关于延续和优化新能源汽车车辆购置税减免政策的公告
title_english: Announcement on Extending and Optimising the Vehicle Purchase Tax Exemption for New Energy Vehicles
summary_english: Exempts new energy vehicles bought in 2024-2025 from vehicle purchase tax, capped at CNY 30,000 per passenger car, and halves the tax for purchases in 2026-2027, capped at CNY 15,000. It covers battery electric, plug-in hybrid (including range-extended) and fuel cell vehicles meeting MIIT technical requirements.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Signing date 2023-06-19 from general knowledge and the release date; check on the official text. Technical requirements adjusted by MIIT/MOF/STA announcement 2023 No. 32 (not recorded).

title_english: New Energy Vehicle Industry Development Plan (2021-2035)
summary_english: Sets a target for new energy vehicles to reach about 20% of new car sales by 2025 and for battery electric vehicles to become the mainstream of new sales over about 15 years. It covers technology development, charging and hydrogen supply infrastructure and full electrification of public-sector fleets.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Signed 2020-10-20, published 2020-11-02 on gov.cn.

title_english: Mineral Resources Law of the PRC (revised 2024)
summary_english: A full revision of the 1986 Mineral Resources Law, expanded from seven chapters and 53 articles to eight chapters and 80 articles. It reorganises mining rights and their competitive allocation, adds a chapter on mine-site ecological restoration and adds provisions on mineral reserves and emergency response.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Presidential Order No. 36 of 2024-11-08 (gov.cn); in force 2025-07-01. Check for provisions on strategic minerals and international resource cooperation. The 1986 law and 1996/2009 amendments are not recorded.

title_english: Regulations on the Administration of Rare Earths
summary_english: Regulates rare earth mining, smelting and separation, metal smelting, comprehensive use, product circulation and import and export. It declares rare earth resources state-owned, makes MIIT responsible for the industry and provides for total quantity control and product traceability.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Adopted at the State Council executive meeting of 2024-04-26, signed 2024-06-22, in force 2024-10-01. Total-quantity-control and traceability details from summaries; check the articles.

title_english: Interim Measures for the Total Quantity Control of Rare Earth Mining and Smelting and Separation
summary_english: Applies total quantity control to rare earth mining and to smelting and separation, including of imported ore and monazite. Annual quotas are proposed by MIIT with MNR and NDRC, approved by the State Council and allocated to designated enterprises, which must record product flows in a traceability system.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Published by MIIT on 2025-08-22; in force on promulgation. Per the State Council Gazette version, revokes the 2012 interim measures on mandatory rare earth production plans (not recorded).

title_english: Foreign Investment Law of the PRC
summary_english: Establishes pre-establishment national treatment plus a negative list for foreign investment, replacing the three earlier laws on foreign-invested enterprises. It provides for investment protection and a foreign investment security review mechanism.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Order number and dates confirmed by search summaries of the official text; flk.npc.gov.cn did not answer. Security review provision and the replacement of the three earlier laws are from general knowledge; check. Implementing regulations (State Council Order No. 723, 2019) and the 2020 Security Review Measures not recorded.

summary_english: Reduces the nationwide negative list for foreign investment from 31 to 29 measures and removes all remaining restrictions in manufacturing. Sectors outside the list are open to foreign investment on the same terms as domestic investment; it replaces the 2021 edition.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Release date 2024-09-08 from NDRC and media summaries; the gov.cn page was not opened, so the signing date on the order must be checked. title_english: Standard Conditions for the Photovoltaic Manufacturing Industry (2024 Edition)
summary_english: Sets conditions for polysilicon, ingot, wafer, cell, module and inverter manufacturers to be listed by MIIT, including a minimum 30% capital ratio for new and expanded projects, cell and module efficiency thresholds and a 12-year process and materials warranty. It discourages projects that only expand capacity and replaces the 2021 edition (MIIT announcement 2021 No. 5).
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). The text describes itself as guidance without prerequisite or mandatory force for administrative approval, so binding = no. Announcement number from local government copies; date 2024-11-15 on copies, 2024-11-20 per Fujian MIIT report. URL is MIIT's interpretation page. title_original: 财政部 税务总局关于调整出口退税政策的公告
title_english: Announcement on Adjusting Export Tax Rebate Policies
summary_english: Cuts the VAT export rebate rate from 13% to 9% for some refined oil products, photovoltaic products, batteries and some non-metallic mineral products, and removes the rebate for aluminium and copper products. Rates apply by the export date on the customs declaration.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). PV and battery rates changed again by CN-DEC-MOF-2026-2. Topic fit: export rebates are recorded under manufacturing-incentives as a fiscal support to exporters; reviewers may prefer a trade topic. Check HS code lists in annex 2.

title_english: Announcement on Adjusting Export Tax Rebate Policies for Photovoltaic and Other Products
summary_english: Removes the VAT export rebate for photovoltaic and other listed products from 2026-04-01. For battery products it cuts the rebate from 9% to 6% for 2026-04-01 to 2026-12-31 and removes it from 2027-01-01.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Dated 2026-01-08, published 2026-01-09. Annex lists reportedly 249 PV-related and 22 battery tariff lines (secondary). The battery step to zero takes effect 2027-01-01.

summary_english: Provides the legal basis for control lists, licensing and end-use and end-user controls on exports of dual-use items, military products and nuclear items, including temporary controls. It is the basis for the MOFCOM and GAC announcements on critical minerals and battery items recorded here.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). npc.gov.cn and MOFCOM copies located by search; not opened.

title_english: Regulations of the PRC on Export Control of Dual-Use Items
summary_english: Implements the Export Control Law for dual-use items in six chapters and 50 articles, covering the control list, temporary controls, licensing conditions, end-user and end-use management and a watch list. It abolishes the registration requirement for dual-use exporters.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Adopted 2024-09-18, signed 2024-09-30, in force 2024-12-01. A unified Dual-Use Items Export Control List took effect on the same date (not recorded).

summary_english: Requires an export licence for listed gallium items (including metal, gallium nitride and gallium oxide) and germanium items. Licences are issued by MOFCOM, with State Council approval where required.

summary_english: Requires an export licence for high-purity, high-strength, high-density synthetic graphite and its products and for natural flake graphite and its products, including spherical and expanded graphite. It lifts temporary controls on five low-sensitivity graphite items and repeals MOFCOM-COSTIND-GAC announcement 2006 No. 50.

summary_english: Requires an export licence for antimony ores and raw materials, antimony metal and products, antimony oxides and some compounds, related smelting and separation technology, and superhard material items. Licences for listed items require State Council approval.

summary_english: Requires an export licence for items related to seven medium and heavy rare earths (samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium and yttrium), including metals, alloys, oxides, compounds and samarium-cobalt magnets.

summary_english: Requires foreign entities to obtain a MOFCOM dual-use export licence before exporting from third countries items made abroad that contain Chinese-origin rare earth content or use Chinese rare earth technology. Applications for military end users are in principle refused.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Parts were to apply from publication and parts from 2025-12-01 per MOFCOM summaries; check. Suspended by 2025 No. 70 and CN-DEC-MOFCOM-2026-58 until 2027-01-10.

summary_english: Places under dual-use export control technologies for rare earth mining, smelting and separation, metal smelting, magnet manufacturing (samarium-cobalt, NdFeB and cerium magnets) and recycling, and for assembling and maintaining production lines. Export covers transfers by trade, licensing, investment, training, joint research and employment.

summary_english: Omnibus infrastructure law. title_original: An Act to ensure that goods made with forced labor in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of the People's Republic of China do not enter the United States market, and for other purposes
title_english: An Act to ensure that goods made with forced labor in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of the People's Republic of China do not enter the United States market, and for other purposes
summary_english: Creates a rebuttable presumption that goods mined, produced or manufactured wholly or in part in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, or by listed entities, are made with forced labour and barred from import under section 307 of the Tariff Act of 1930. Importers can rebut the presumption only with clear and convincing evidence; the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force maintains an entity list and enforcement strategy.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Approval date and the 180-day commencement of the section 3 presumption read from the govinfo text; date_in_force computed as 180 days after enactment (2022-06-21), check. Polysilicon is a priority sector in DHS enforcement (from secondary knowledge; DHS and CBP UFLPA pages returned 403). Mapped to import-standards as an import prohibition; no topic covers forced-labour bans exactly.

title_english: An Act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of S. Con. Res. 14 (Inflation Reduction Act of 2022)
summary_english: Budget reconciliation law that created or extended clean energy tax credits, including the clean vehicle credit with critical mineral and battery component sourcing rules (section 13401, Code 30D), the advanced manufacturing production credit for solar, wind, inverter, battery components and critical minerals (section 13502, Code 45X) and technology-neutral clean electricity production and investment credits (sections 13701-13702, Code 45Y and 48E) with domestic content bonus amounts. It also allowed transfer and elective payment of credits.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Approval date and section numbers read from govinfo text. Amended by US-PL-2025-119-21 (termination of 30D, phase-out of 45X, termination of 45Y/48E for wind and solar, prohibited foreign entity rules). Other IRA programmes (e.g. DOE loan authority, methane emissions charge) not recorded.

title_original: An Act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14 (One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act)
title_english: An Act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14 (One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act)
summary_english: Budget reconciliation law whose title VII, chapter 5 amends the Inflation Reduction Act credits. It ends the 30D clean vehicle credit for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025; ends 45Y and 48E for wind and solar facilities placed in service after 2027 unless construction begins within 12 months of enactment; ends 45X for wind components sold after 2027 and phases it out for critical minerals from 2031; and denies credits to specified foreign entities and to facilities or components with material assistance from a prohibited foreign entity.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Sections 70502, 70512, 70513 and 70514 read from the govinfo text (approved July 4, 2025). Effective dates vary by section; date_in_force set to enactment. Reviewer: confirm the 45X phase-out schedule for components other than critical minerals and the material-assistance cost ratio thresholds, which were not read in full.

title_original: Beginning of Construction Requirements for Purposes of the Termination of Clean Electricity Production Credits and Clean Electricity Investment Credits for Applicable Wind and Solar Facilities
title_english: Beginning of Construction Requirements for Purposes of the Termination of Clean Electricity Production Credits and Clean Electricity Investment Credits for Applicable Wind and Solar Facilities
summary_english: Guidance, issued under Executive Order 14315, on when construction of a wind or solar facility begins for the OBBBA termination of the 45Y and 48E credits. It requires the physical work test and removes the five percent cost safe harbour except for solar facilities of 1.5 MW or less, and keeps a four-year continuity safe harbour.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Effective date (facilities not begun before 2025-09-02) and 1.5 MW exception read from the IRS PDF. Release date 2025-08-15 from law-firm notes (EY, KPMG). Modifies Notice 2022-61 for this purpose (not recorded).

short_name: Interim guidance on material assistance from prohibited foreign entities
issuing_body: Department of the Treasury; Internal Revenue Service
title_original: Guidance to Apply Interim Safe Harbors for Purposes of Determining a Taxpayer's Material Assistance from a Prohibited Foreign Entity; Other Prohibited Foreign Entity Guidance
title_english: Guidance to Apply Interim Safe Harbors for Purposes of Determining a Taxpayer's Material Assistance from a Prohibited Foreign Entity; Other Prohibited Foreign Entity Guidance
summary_english: Interim guidance on the OBBBA prohibited foreign entity restrictions for the 45X, 45Y and 48E credits. It sets out how to compute the material assistance cost ratio for qualified facilities, energy storage technology and eligible components, with interim safe harbours, ahead of proposed regulations.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Title and purpose read from the IRS PDF. Release date 2026-02-12 from secondary sources (EY, KPMG). Reviewer: check whether proposed regulations on PFE determinations have since been issued.

short_name: DOE interpretation of foreign entity of concern
title_original: Interpretation of Foreign Entity of Concern
title_english: Interpretation of Foreign Entity of Concern
summary_english: Final interpretive rule on the statutory definition of 'foreign entity of concern' in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which applies to DOE battery supply chain programmes. It clarifies when an entity is owned by, controlled by or subject to the jurisdiction or direction of the government of a covered nation; Treasury relies on the definition for the 30D credit.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). From the Federal Register API abstract (proposed 2023-12-04). Reviewer: confirm the 25 percent control threshold and covered nations from the rule text.

short_name: Section 201 safeguard on CSPV cells and modules
title_original: To Facilitate Positive Adjustment to Competition From Imports of Certain Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Cells (Whether or Not Partially or Fully Assembled Into Other Products) and for Other Purposes
title_english: To Facilitate Positive Adjustment to Competition From Imports of Certain Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Cells (Whether or Not Partially or Fully Assembled Into Other Products) and for Other Purposes
summary_english: Safeguard measure under section 201 of the Trade Act of 1974 on crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells and modules for four years: a tariff-rate quota on cells and an additional duty on modules, both declining annually. Modified by Proclamation 10101 (2020) and extended by Proclamation 10339 (2022).
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). 83 FR 3541; effective 12:01 a.m. 2018-02-07 read from govinfo text. First-year rates (30 percent, 2.5 GW cell quota) are from general knowledge; check Annex I. Proclamation 10101 (85 FR 65639, 2020-10-10; revoked bifacial exclusion, raised fourth-year rate to 18 percent) not recorded as a row. Status 'expired' because the extended measure ran to the eight-year statutory maximum (see US-PROC-2022-10339).

title_original: To Continue Facilitating Positive Adjustment to Competition From Imports of Certain Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Cells (Whether or Not Partially or Fully Assembled Into Other Products)
title_english: To Continue Facilitating Positive Adjustment to Competition From Imports of Certain Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Cells (Whether or Not Partially or Fully Assembled Into Other Products)
summary_english: Extends the solar safeguard for four more years with a 5.0 GW annual cell tariff-rate quota and declining module duties, and excludes bifacial panels. Later proclamations revoked the bifacial exclusion (Proclamation 10779, June 2024) and raised the cell quota to 12.5 GW from 1 August 2024 (Proclamation 10790).
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). 87 FR 7357; 5.0 GW quota and bifacial exclusion read from govinfo text. Proclamations 10779 (89 FR 53333) and 10790 (89 FR 66181, 12.5 GW from 2024-08-01) read but not recorded as rows. End date 2026-02-06 inferred from the eight-year limit in Trade Act section 203(e)(1)(A) and the 2018-02-07 start; no termination notice was located. Confirm on USITC/CBP.

short_name: Solar duty pause for Southeast Asia
title_original: Declaration of Emergency and Authorization for Temporary Extensions of Time and Duty-Free Importation of Solar Cells and Modules From Southeast Asia
title_english: Declaration of Emergency and Authorization for Temporary Extensions of Time and Duty-Free Importation of Solar Cells and Modules From Southeast Asia
summary_english: Declares an emergency on electricity generation capacity under section 318(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 and allows duty-free importation of solar cells and modules from Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, free of any antidumping or countervailing duties that might result from the circumvention inquiry, for 24 months or until the emergency ends.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). 87 FR 35067; 24-month period read from govinfo text, ending 2024-06-06. Commerce implementing rule (Sept 2022) and the 180-day utilisation condition not recorded; check. A 2023 CRA resolution to overturn it was vetoed (from secondary knowledge).

short_name: Section 232 action on processed critical minerals
title_original: Adjusting Imports of Processed Critical Minerals and Their Derivative Products Into The United States
title_english: Adjusting Imports of Processed Critical Minerals and Their Derivative Products Into The United States
summary_english: Acts on the Commerce section 232 investigation into processed critical minerals and derivative products, opened under Executive Order 14272 (April 2025). Instead of tariffs, it directs the Secretary of Commerce and the Trade Representative to pursue negotiated agreements with trading partners and reserves other measures, including minimum import prices, if negotiations do not succeed.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). 91 FR 2439; operative clauses skimmed in govinfo text (negotiation, no tariff). Reviewer: read in full for any immediate measures and deadlines; USTR requested comments on a plurilateral critical minerals agreement (91 FR 9686, 2026-02-26).

short_name: Section 232 measures on polysilicon and derivatives
title_original: Adjusting Imports of Polysilicon and Its Derivatives Into the United States
title_english: Adjusting Imports of Polysilicon and Its Derivatives Into the United States
summary_english: From 4 December 2026, sets minimum import prices for polysilicon ($21/kg), ingots and wafers ($100/kg), solar cells ($0.22/W) and modules ($0.38/W), with a specific tariff where entries fall below them, plus an additional 15 percent duty on ingots and derivatives in the annexes. Lower combined caps apply to some partners, and Commerce may approve onshoring plans.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). 91 FR 51975; prices, 15 percent duty and 2026-12-04 start read from govinfo text. BIS temporary final rule restricting stockpiling (91 FR 60505, effective 2026-09-22 to 2026-12-03) not recorded. Reviewer: check annex coverage (whether polysilicon itself bears the 15 percent) and partner caps (Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, EU, UK).

title_original: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
title_english: Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
summary_english: Imposes, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, an additional 10 percent ad valorem duty on imports from all trading partners from 5 April 2025 and higher country-specific rates from 9 April 2025, later modified by further orders. Goods in Annex II, including certain critical minerals and energy and energy products, were excluded.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). 90 FR 15041; dates and Annex II categories read from govinfo text. Many amending orders (e.g. 14259, 14266) not recorded. The Supreme Court held on 2026-02-20 (Learning Resources v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs (secondary sources); collection ended under US-EO-2026-14389. Refund process not researched.

title_original: Ending Certain Tariff Actions
title_english: Ending Certain Tariff Actions
summary_english: Terminates the additional ad valorem duties imposed under earlier IEEPA executive orders, including Executive Order 14257 as amended, and directs agencies to end their collection.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). 91 FR 9437; list of terminated orders read from govinfo text. Issued the day of the Supreme Court decision; reviewer to confirm the effective time of termination.

title_original: Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge To Address Fundamental International Payments Problems
title_english: Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge To Address Fundamental International Payments Problems
summary_english: Imposes, under section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, a 10 percent ad valorem surcharge on imports for 150 days from 24 February 2026. Certain critical minerals, energy and energy products, certain electronics, and passenger and other vehicles and parts are excluded.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). 91 FR 9339; rate, period and exclusions read from govinfo text. Status 'expired' assumes the 150-day statutory limit ran out (about 2026-07-23) without extension by Congress; not confirmed. USTR section 301 tariffs on 60 economies (forced labour enforcement) apply from 2026-07-24 (91 FR 47318), not recorded; check their clean-tech exemptions.

title_original: Unleashing American Energy
title_english: Unleashing American Energy
summary_english: Sets an energy policy favouring domestic fossil fuel, mineral and nuclear production and directs agencies to review regulations burdening energy production. Section 7 orders agencies to pause disbursement of funds under the Inflation Reduction Act and the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, including EV charging funds, pending review, and the order states a policy to eliminate the 'electric vehicle mandate'.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). 90 FR 8353; section 7 read from govinfo text. Court rulings on the funding pause (secondary sources) not researched; check.

short_name: Immediate measures to increase American mineral production
title_original: Immediate Measures To Increase American Mineral Production
title_english: Immediate Measures To Increase American Mineral Production
summary_english: Directs agencies to identify priority mineral production projects and expedite permits, to use Defense Production Act section 303 authority and to add mineral production as a priority under the Act, and to use development finance tools to support domestic mineral production and processing.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). 90 FR 13673; sections read from govinfo text. Amended by Executive Order 14261 (2025-04-08, adds coal), not recorded. EO 14285 (offshore critical minerals, 2025-04-24) not recorded.

short_name: Ending subsidies for foreign-controlled energy sources
title_original: Ending Market Distorting Subsidies for Unreliable, Foreign-Controlled Energy Sources
title_english: Ending Market Distorting Subsidies for Unreliable, Foreign-Controlled Energy Sources
summary_english: Directs the Treasury, within 45 days of enactment of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, to strictly enforce the termination of the 45Y and 48E credits for wind and solar, including beginning-of-construction guidance, and to implement the foreign entity of concern restrictions. Directs the Interior to remove preferences for wind and solar.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). 90 FR 30821; sections 2-5 read from govinfo text.

short_name: DPA Title III determination for large-capacity batteries
title_original: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended
title_english: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended
summary_english: Determines under section 303 of the Defense Production Act that strategic and critical materials for the large-capacity battery supply chain, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, graphite and manganese, are essential to national defence, which allows Title III funding for feasibility studies, production and processing.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). 87 FR 19775; minerals list read from govinfo text.

short_name: DPA section 101 determination on recoverable critical minerals
title_original: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 101 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Recoverable Critical Minerals and Materials
title_english: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 101 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Recoverable Critical Minerals and Materials
summary_english: Finds under section 101 of the Defense Production Act that recoverable critical minerals and materials, including black mass, end-of-life rare-earth permanent magnets, swarf and other scrap containing critical minerals, are scarce and critical materials essential to national defence, and authorises the Secretary of Commerce to issue regulations to implement the finding.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). 91 FR 50465; text read from govinfo. Implementing Commerce rules (possible allocation or export limits on scrap and black mass) not located; check.

title_original: Notice of Action and Request for Public Comment Concerning Proposed Determination of Action Pursuant to Section 301: China's Acts, Policies, and Practices Related to Technology Transfer, Intellectual Property, and Innovation
title_english: Notice of Action and Request for Public Comment Concerning Proposed Determination of Action Pursuant to Section 301: China's Acts, Policies, and Practices Related to Technology Transfer, Intellectual Property, and Innovation
summary_english: First action in the section 301 investigation of China's technology transfer practices: an additional 25 percent duty on products of China in Annex A, with a product exclusion process. Later lists extended duties to most imports from China.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Rate and annex from the Federal Register abstract. Effective date 2018-07-06 from general knowledge; check. Lists 2-4A (2018-2019) not recorded. Which clean-tech HTS lines were in List 1 versus later lists not checked.

issuing_body: Office of the United States Trade Representative
title_original: Notice of Modification: China's Acts, Policies and Practices Related to Technology Transfer, Intellectual Property and Innovation
title_english: Notice of Modification: China's Acts, Policies and Practices Related to Technology Transfer, Intellectual Property and Innovation
summary_english: Raises section 301 duties on products of China in strategic sectors: electric vehicles to 100 percent and solar cells (whether or not in modules) to 50 percent from 2024; lithium-ion EV batteries, non-lithium battery parts and other critical minerals to 25 percent from 2024; lithium-ion non-EV batteries, natural graphite and permanent magnets to 25 percent from 2026.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Rates read from the govinfo text. A follow-up notice (89 FR 101682, 2024-12-16) raised rates on polysilicon, wafers and certain tungsten products from 2025-01-01 (rate of 50 percent for polysilicon and wafers from secondary knowledge; check), not recorded as a row.

title_english: Certain Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Products From the People's Republic of China: Antidumping Duty Order; and Amended Final Affirmative Countervailing Duty Determination and Countervailing Duty Order; Certain Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Products From Taiwan: Antidumping Duty Order

title_original: Improvements to Generator Interconnection Procedures and Agreements
title_english: Improvements to Generator Interconnection Procedures and Agreements
summary_english: Revises FERC's pro forma large and small generator interconnection procedures and agreements to address interconnection queue backlogs, replacing serial studies with cluster studies and adding readiness requirements, study deadlines and provisions for new technologies such as storage.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Citation and effective date from the Federal Register API; issuance date 2023-07-27 and the cluster-study detail from general knowledge (ferc.gov returned 403). Order No. 2023-A (89 FR 27006, 2024-04-16) not recorded.

title_english: Building for the Future Through Electric Regional Transmission Planning and Cost Allocation

notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). Citation and effective date from the Federal Register API; issuance date 2024-05-13 from general knowledge. Orders 1920-A (89 FR 97174, 2024-12-06) and 1920-B (90 FR 17692, 2025-04-28) not recorded. Appeals pending (secondary knowledge); check.

short_name: 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards for power plants
title_original: New Source Performance Standards for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From New, Modified, and Reconstructed Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units; Emission Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Existing Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units; and Repeal of the Affordable Clean Energy Rule
title_english: New Source Performance Standards for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From New, Modified, and Reconstructed Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units; Emission Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Emissions From Existing Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units; and Repeal of the Affordable Clean Energy Rule
summary_english: Clean Air Act section 111 rule that repealed the Affordable Clean Energy rule, set emission guidelines for existing coal and oil/gas steam generating units and revised performance standards for new combustion turbines and modified coal units, with carbon capture-based standards for long-running units.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence). From the Federal Register API abstract (date_signed = publication date). Carbon capture details from general knowledge. Mostly repealed by US-EPA-2026-CPS-REPEAL. Mapped to carbon-pricing for want of a GHG-standards topic; reviewer to decide.

short_name: Partial repeal of 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards
title_original: Partial Repeal of the Carbon Pollution Standards for Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
title_english: Partial Repeal of the Carbon Pollution Standards for Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
summary_english: Repeals most provisions of the 2024 standards: the emission guidelines for existing fossil steam generating units, the carbon capture-based standards for coal units undertaking large modifications and the carbon capture-based (phase 2) standards for new base load combustion turbines. A concurrent supplemental proposal seeks comment on rescinding all GHG requirements for these units.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Abstract and effective date (2026-11-16) from the Federal Register API. The June 2025 proposal (90 FR 25752) proposed full repeal; the concurrent proposal is 91 FR 59002. Check litigation.

title_english: Rescission of the Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding and Motor Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Emission Standards Under the Clean Air Act
summary_english: Rescinds the 2009 endangerment and contribution findings under Clean Air Act section 202(a) and repeals all greenhouse gas emission standards for light-, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and engines, including the 2024 model year 2027+ standards.
notes: Scouted from desk research (high confidence). Abstract and effective date from the Federal Register API. NHTSA SAFE III fuel-economy rule (91 FR 61988, effective 2026-11-30) not recorded. Check litigation.

notes: Scouted from desk research (low confidence). Chapter number, dates and targets from general knowledge; leginfo returned 403. Later bill SB 1020 (2022) added interim clean-electricity targets (not recorded); check.

title_english: Decision Revising Net Energy Metering Tariff and Subtariffs

Customers applying for interconnection from 15 April 2023 take service under the new tariff.
notes: Scouted from desk research (medium confidence).
